description: We are a team of Aerospace Engineering and Mathematics students with a shared passion for problem-solving and mathematical modeling. Our group combines a strong analytical mindset with hands-on technical abilities. We are a highly motivated team ready to tackle whatever problems come our way.
summary: Astrea let's your build your own moon landing mission. Then, it calculates the available landing spots according to real data about the operation. At last, it show's the trajectory of the rocket with its risks at any moment.
details:
Astrea addresses two main challenges related to planning and assessing the viability of future space missions.

Its fundamentals lie in two different objectives.

The first one is to provide an intuitive and interactive interface that allows users to explore potential lunar landing sites for a spacecraft launched from Earth. By visualizing the lunar surface and relevant mission data, users can easily compare different landing locations and understand the factors that make each site suitable for a mission.

The second objective is to develop new methods for calculating the risks associated with space operations at a low computational cost. These include smooth piece-wise interpolation of astronomical trajectories, quantization validated by mathematical bounding, or discrete estimation of continuous functions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

On the one hand, processing huge amounts of data fed through an easy-to-use interactive interface vastly helps users understand and visualize complex space missions. Moreover, the non-linear risk assessment scoring component introduces a more systematic approach to evaluating mission viability.

On the other hand, the complex methods used to efficiently calculate complex mission parameters at scale will contribute new perspectives and optimization techniques for tackling similar problems.

The impact is clear: contributing to safer, faster, more informed, and more efficient space exploration.

Creativity and Innovation

The project seeks to bridge the gap between complex scientific data and human understanding with a traditional analytical interface.

The interface also comes with a Virtual Reality function, making use of phones' gyroscopic sensors. The feature can be tested on any mobile device and will provide an interactive experience, locating the user on any point of the Moon's surface thus enhancing the immersion.

Technical details

This project uses multiple NASA data sources in order to create a truthful and realistic application. The main languages used for development were Python for backend functions and TypeScript for web development. On these foundations multiple other libraries were used for various functionalities, such as 3D rendering, efficient mathematical computation or image processing. Regarding mathematical tools, areas such as probability, multivariate calculus or differential equation solving were crucial in the construction of the framework for numerical quantities.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Astrea is its foundation in real data. Every exploration and assessment is connected to actual information about the Moon and space missions. Our aim is not simply to create another visualization tool, but to demonstrate how real data, mathematics, and accessible technology can come together to bring space exploration closer to the people on Earth.
